**WARNING:** "the owner rebases on `enter`" promises behavior `bro work enter` doesn't have

`work enter` never rebases — `cmdEnter` in `packages/cli/src/commands/work.ts` creates the worktree+branch or checks out an existing branch, and the file contains no rebase path; the Plan below adds none either. As written, the sync contract's escape hatch for dirty/locked worktrees points at a mechanism that doesn't exist, so skipped children silently never catch up. Either state that the owner rebases by hand before continuing, or add a plan item for an explicit rebase step on `enter`.

```suggestion
  touched: sync skips it and reports; the owner rebases manually.
```

**SUGGESTION:** "worktree first, then branch" isn't an orderable step pair via the primitive this spec mandates

The spec says `stack push` reuses `bro work enter --base <tip> --branch <name>` (above and in the Plan), but `enter` creates the worktree and branch in one atomic `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <base>` (`cmdEnter` in `packages/cli/src/commands/work.ts`) — they cannot be sequenced. The failure-safe contract is really two steps (worktree+branch atomically, registry edge last); describing three ordered steps sends the implementer either outside `enter` (contradicting "no new flag") or into a guarantee that doesn't exist.

**SUGGESTION:** Template puts three `##` sections on one line — copied verbatim it renders as a single malformed heading

In Markdown a heading ends at the newline, so `## Result …  ## Prevention …  ## Trail (children, evidence links)` is one heading whose text swallows the other two. This fence is the template the "report template + frontmatter writer" plan item implements, so put each `##` section on its own line.
